title: Ultrahigh output triboelectric nanogenerators  via  dual-domain charge bootstrapping strategy
content: Triboelectric nanogenerators (TENGs) offer a promising approach for mechanical energy harvesting and distributed power supply. However, limited triboelectric charge density and the mismatch between charge accumulation and useful charge extraction still restrict their energy output. A dual-domain charge bootstrapping (DCB) strategy is proposed, which decouples external charge transport paths while preserving electrostatic coupling and effectively extracting electrostatic energy from both charge domains, thereby achieving both high charge accumulation and efficient energy utilization. Furthermore, the charge retention characteristics of the charge confinement structure and its dynamic regulation for dual-channel output are elucidated. Leveraging this method, compared with the initial triboelectrification state, the transfer charge and stored energy increase by 187.3-fold and 5736.2-fold, respectively. An integrated prototype using DCB achieves a volume charge density of up to 10.95 mC m−3 and a peak power density of 233.34 W m−3 at a frequency of 1 Hz. After power management, the prototype can light up 75 bulbs, each rated at 3 W. This work provides a new design framework for ultrahigh output TENGs.
